variants.value: d_cat<=3.5px; fixed-count FIFO-BFS H19-5 refill; min d_cat>3.5px

mechanism_card.hypothesis: At d_cat<=3.5 px, R0's near-catalogue flank dots contain more false-positive mass than new-fault credit; replacing that collar with the same lineage's next-ranked ridge pixels should improve DTI without changing the emitted mass.
mechanism_card.mechanism: Known catalogue pixels are masked pixel-exactly, while a nearby new fault remains scoreable; the PRUNE edit tests whether the empirical 2.0 px collar is too narrow. It drops every parent dot inside the specified radius and replaces the exact count from the H19-5 support, using its recovered FIFO-BFS thinning order, only where d_cat is strictly outside the new collar.
mechanism_card.non_fault_confounder: H19-5's next-priority pixels may be ridges from lithologic contacts, drainage margins, or topographic lineaments rather than faults; new-fault truth may also cluster beside known traces.
mechanism_card.predicted_live_change: +0.002 DTI (MODEL; plausible interval -0.010 to +0.010; not a score)
mechanism_card.falsifier: A paired, same-week live receipt against R0 with Δ<=-0.010 falsifies the proposed positive collar effect for this cutoff/refill policy. Any |Δ|<0.010 is no evidence under the session rule.
mechanism_card.structural_geologist_note: Interpret this as a positional-uncertainty/collar experiment, not as a claim that faults do not continue near mapped traces. Review both removed flanks and FIFO-ranked refill ridges on geology.

variants.value: cross-strike consensus(TMI hg, iso-grav hg) cap 1 px, half-angle 45 deg, min sep 2 px

mechanism_card.hypothesis: Correcting cross-strike position by up to 1 px moves dots toward the strongest magnetic/gravity gradient edge, which is where a mapped fault trace is most likely to lie; because kernel credit is linear in distance, this raises T without adding mass.
mechanism_card.mechanism: GeoDAWN Area 2 was flown at 400 m line spacing 150-200 m above terrain, so a lineament's dominant positional error is across strike and of order the 300 m (3 px) kernel radius. The consensus of two independent supplied gradient bands (tmi_hg, iso_grav_anom_hg) is used only as a within-2 px tie-breaker along each dot's local normal (PCA of its 8 nearest parent dots). 0 of 37,654 dots moved; mean displacement 0.00 px. The shared collar step removed 1,611 parent dots inside 3 px of the catalogue and refilled the same count from the H19-5 pool, so every arm is identical apart from the dose.
mechanism_card.non_fault_confounder: Lithologic contacts, drainage margins and culture edges also produce magnetic and gravity gradients; a dot can be pulled onto one of those and away from a real fault. The consensus of two independent physical fields reduces, but does not remove, single-source artefacts.
mechanism_card.falsifier: Paired same-week live receipt against R0: Delta <= -0.010 falsifies the cross-strike alignment mechanism at 1 px; any |Delta| < 0.010 is no evidence under the session rule. A dose ordering that is not monotone in the cap also falsifies the 'closer to the edge is better' reading, because the two larger caps nest the smaller one.
mechanism_card.structural_geologist_note: Judge whether the moved dots sit on a plausible fault trace or on a stratigraphic contact: the edit never adds mass, so any gain or loss is purely positional. The rank-normalised consensus is a relative edge strength, not a fault probability.
